newsitem.title: USA: Fore wins major French Libary network contract.
newsitem.headline: Fore wins major French Libary network contract.

text.p: Fore Systems Inc. said Wednesday it was selected by the French National Library to build Europe's largest end-to-end network using high speed technology for delivering multimedia text, voice and video.
It said the network will link multiple branches of the French National Library, one of the world's oldest public libraries.

In a statement from Paris, Pittsburgh, Pa.-based Fore said the installation will include 300 of its high-speed asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) computer network switches and connect more than 3,500 workstation users on a network capable of sending multimedia data at speeds of up 155 megabits per second.
A Fore spokeswoman said the project represents the largest number of users with direct ATM connections that Fore has ever announced.
ATM technology is a high speed method for delivering multimedia text, voice and video, which many analysts consider to represent the future of office computer network technology.
The ATM network will be put into operation during the first half of 1997, the company said.

The high-performance ATM network will enable computer users to retrieve digital, multimedia versions of works contained in library archives. The network also will be able to provide services like teleconferencing and Internet access.
Library officials chose the ATM network for its capacity to provide rapid information access and speed document retrieval time, the company said.

The network will be designed by Fore and implemented by Phillips Communication D'Enterprise, a Fore network integrator and distributor in France. French computer firm Groupe Bull will provide systems integration for the project.
Fore Systems stock was up $1.69 at $40 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
